narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 52.7% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability tipped just above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your academic record. Your class ranking at the end of your third year was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Standing in the second decile is noticeably lower than the average third-year ranking of students who were admitted, and this weaker relative performance strongly signaled higher risk to the model. Your first-year ranking in the third decile also pulled the prediction toward failure, though less dramatically, because it similarly placed you below the typical performance of accepted students.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.30 worked in the opposite direction. It is slightly above the average GPA of admitted students and therefore gave the model some confidence that you could succeed. However, this positive signal was not large enough to overcome the two class-rank indicators.

Taken together, the model concluded that your overall academic trajectory pointed to a slightly elevated chance of struggling with the bar exam. To improve your prospects, focus on raising your class standing in the remaining years and consider targeted bar-preparation resources that address the specific demands measured by those early decile rankings. Strengthening those areas will directly counteract the factors that led to this decision. (218 words)
